paragraphs: There are a few useful things you can do with an old Apple Watch after you upgrade to a new one. You might think of the Apple Watch as being a disposable product — because who would wear two watches? But there are actually quite a few surprising use cases for having a daily Apple Watch and a secondary watch.

Upgrading your Apple Watch doesn’t have to mean consigning the old one to a junk drawer. In fact, that older wearable could turn out to be incredibly useful once it’s no longer your everyday companion.

The Apple Watch is a surprisingly capable little computer, and keeping a second one around opens up some clever possibilities. You might use it as a dedicated sleep tracker, a beater for risky adventures, or even a stripped-down phone for leaving your iPhone behind. In a world where tech companies constantly encourage us to trade up, sometimes finding a second life for a gadget you already own can mean a real lifestyle upgrade.

The Apple Watch is great for tracking sleep — even the different stages of your sleep through the night. And if you use your Apple Watch as an alarm, it’ll wake you up by silently buzzing on your wrist, so your partner won’t be awoken by your alarm if they wake up a little later.

However, if you wear your watch during the day and you wear it to bed, when do you charge it? Personally, I hate the idea of charging my watch during the day because if I get up and move around while it’s juicing up, I won’t get credit for my Move or Stand rings.

This points to a prime way to put an old Apple Watch to good use: Turn it into a dedicated sleep tracker and alarm. You keep your old one on the charger during the day and wear your new one out and about. Then, you swap them when it’s time for bed and after you wake up. You never need to worry about topping up the battery in the evening before you go to sleep or in the morning rush.

Another benefit? If your daily watch band focuses on fashion rather than comfort, like a Milanese Loop, you don’t need to switch it out with a Sport Band every morning and every night. You can pick the best type of band for each Apple Watch.

The Apple Watch is surprisingly hardy and water-resistant, but sometimes an unusual excursion might make you a bit nervous about wearing it. Instead of risking your expensive new Apple Watch when you go rock climbing, skydiving or swimming in the ocean, you can strap on your old watch instead. After all, a hand-me-down Apple Watch is much cheaper than buying a new Apple Watch Ultra.
